chunks: And from him from Abdullah ibn al-Salt said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the young girl whose father marries her off: Does she have authority (choice) when she reaches puberty? He said, 'No.' And I asked him about the virgin when she reaches the maturity of women: Does she have authority with her father? He said, 'She does not have authority with her father unless she is married off (thayyib) [by herself or has choice].'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he contracted the marriage for her while she was young, she does not have the option (of annulment) upon reaching puberty. The preceding report from Abdullah ibn al-Salt indicates this, and also what he narrated:

key_terms.تُثَيَّبْ: she is made a thayyib (married off with choice)

ai.seo_question: Does a young girl have the right to choose her husband if her father marries her off before she reaches puberty?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *khiyar al-bulugh* (option of puberty) for a *bikr* (virgin) married by her father. It establishes the principle that a father’s marriage of his minor daughter is binding without her subsequent consent, distinguishing this from cases where the daughter herself acts as her own wali. This ruling underscores the patriarchal authority in Shia jurisprudence regarding the marriage of minors, provided the marriage contract was validly executed during minority.
